# BurgerAPI - Bun-native API Framework

> BurgerAPI is a Bun-first, WinterCG-compatible API framework with file-based routing, six lifecycle hooks, plugins, providers, Standard Schema (Zod) validation, automatic OpenAPI generation, shared `BurgerContext`, and WebSocket support. It ships as two packages, `burger-api` (`1.0.0-beta.2`) and `@burger-api/cli` (`1.0.0-beta.4`) (public beta; feedback welcome at GitHub issues). TypeScript and JavaScript are both first-class, and the same app runs on Bun, Node, Cloudflare Workers, Deno, and Vercel.

## Table of Contents

### Overview

- [Introduction](https://burger-api.com/docs/): BurgerAPI is a Bun-first framework for building APIs.

### Getting Started

- [Quick Start](https://burger-api.com/docs/quick-start): Get a BurgerAPI app running in under a minute.
- [Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/installation): BurgerAPI runs on Bun.
- [CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli): The burger-api CLI creates projects, adds hooks and plugins, runs your app while you develop, and builds it for production.
- [Key Concepts](https://burger-api.com/docs/key-concepts): These are the main ideas in BurgerAPI.
- [JavaScript](https://burger-api.com/docs/javascript): You can write a BurgerAPI app in JavaScript.
- [Migrating from 0.9.x](https://burger-api.com/docs/migration): This guide is for apps running burger-api 0.9.x and @burger-api/cli 0.9.x.

### Core Concepts

- [Applications](https://burger-api.com/docs/core-concepts/applications): A BurgerAPI app is an instance of the Burger class.
- [Routing](https://burger-api.com/docs/core-concepts/routing): BurgerAPI uses file-based routing.
- [Handlers](https://burger-api.com/docs/core-concepts/handlers): A route file exports one function per HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH.
- [Request Context](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/request-handling): Every handler and hook gets ctx, a BurgerContext.
- [Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/core-concepts/hooks): Hooks run your code at fixed points of a request.
- [Providers](https://burger-api.com/docs/core-concepts/providers): A provider is a service your app shares across requests: a database client, a mailer, a cache.
- [Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/core-concepts/validation): Describe the request you expect with a schema.
- [Configuration](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/configuration): Settings live in a few files, each for one job:
- [Response Types](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/response-types): Handlers return a standard Web Response.

### Routing

- [File-Based Routing](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/file-based-routing): In BurgerAPI, folders under your apiDir become URL paths.
- [Static Routes](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/api/static-routes): A static route has a fixed path, such as /api/products.
- [Route Groups](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/api/route-groups): A route group is a folder name in parentheses, such as (admin).
- [Dynamic Routes](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/api/dynamic-routes): A dynamic route captures part of the URL, such as an ID or a slug.
- [Wildcard Routes](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/api/wildcard-routes): A wildcard route matches every path below a point in the URL.
- [Nested Routes](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/api/nested-routes): Each folder under your apiDir adds one segment to the URL.
- [Static Pages](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/pages/static-pages): BurgerAPI can also serve HTML pages.

### Hooks

- [Hook System](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/system): Hooks let you run code at fixed points of a request.
- [Global Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/global): Global hooks run for every request.
- [Route Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/route-specific): Route hooks run only for one route.
- [Hook Return Types](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/return-types): A hook returns one of three things.
- [After Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/after): afterRoute runs after the handler returns.

### Validation

- [Zod Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/zod): BurgerAPI uses Zod 4 to check requests.
- [Schema Definition](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/schema): Put validation schemas in schema.ts, next to route.ts.
- [Params Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/params): Add a params schema to check path parameters from dynamic folders such as [id].
- [Query Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/query): Add a query schema to a method in schema.ts.
- [Body Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/body): Add a body schema to a method in schema.ts.
- [Headers Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/headers): Add a headers schema to a method in schema.ts.
- [Cookie Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/cookie): Add a cookies schema to a method in schema.ts.
- [Coercion](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/coercion): Query strings, path params, headers and cookies always arrive as text.
- [Response Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/response): Add a response schema to check what your handler returns.
- [Standard Schema Support](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/standard-schema): You can use any schema library that follows Standard Schema, such as Valibot or ArkType.
- [Error Handling](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/errors): When a request fails validation, BurgerAPI answers 422.
- [Problem Details](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/problem-details): By default, a failed request gets a 422 with an application/problem+json body.
- [Validation Config](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/configuration): Set validation options with the validation option of new Burger().
- [Best Practices](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/best-practices): A few habits that keep validation simple.

### WebSocket

- [WebSocket Overview](https://burger-api.com/docs/websocket/overview): WebSocket routes keep a connection open so the server and client can send messages both ways.

### OpenAPI & Documentation

- [OpenAPI / Swagger](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/openapi): BurgerAPI builds an OpenAPI 3.1 document from your routes and schemas.

### Examples

- [Basic Route Example](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/basic-route): A route that answers GET /api/hello:
- [Hello World API](https://burger-api.com/docs/tutorials/hello-world): In this tutorial, you'll create your first BurgerAPI application: a simple "Hello World" API that demonstrates the core concepts of file-based routing and automatic documentation generation.
- [Todo List API](https://burger-api.com/docs/tutorials/todo-api): In this tutorial, you'll build a complete CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) API for managing a todo list.
- [CRUD API](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/crud-api): A products API with list, read, create, update and delete.
- [Blog API](https://burger-api.com/docs/tutorials/blog-api): In this final tutorial, you'll build a sophisticated blog API with multiple related resources (posts and comments), hooks, plugins, nested routes, and advanced features.
- [Authentication](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/authentication): Protect routes with an auth plugin.
- [Pagination](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/pagination): Paginate a list with a validated query, and send the totals as headers.
- [Validation Example](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/validation): Validate the query and body in schema.ts, then read the clean data from ctx.validated.
- [Hooks Example](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/hooks): Export a hook list from src/hooks.ts.
- [Complete Project Example](https://burger-api.com/docs/examples/complete-project): A full BurgerAPI project.

### Ecosystem

- [Introduction](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/introduction): BurgerAPI has a small core.
- [Hooks & Plugins](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/hooks-plugins): The ecosystem has two kinds of packages.
- [CORS Hook](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/cors): This hook adds Access-Control-* headers, so browsers can call your API from another origin.
- [Logger Hook](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/logger): This hook logs each request with its method, URL, status and response time.
- [Rate Limiter](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/rate-limiter): This hook limits how many requests a client can make in a time window.
- [Cache](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/cache): This hook sets the Cache-Control header, so browsers and CDNs know how long they may keep a response.
- [Compression](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/compression): This hook compresses responses with gzip or deflate when the client accepts it.
- [Security Headers](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/security-headers): This hook adds response headers that protect browsers from common attacks, such as HSTS, X-Frame-Options and an optional Content Security Policy (CSP).
- [Timeout](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/timeout): This package limits how long a request may take.
- [Body Size Limiter](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/body-size-limiter): This hook rejects request bodies that are too large.
- [JWT Auth](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/jwt-auth): This plugin reads a JSON Web Token from the Authorization: Bearer header and checks its signature.
- [API Key Auth](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/api-key-auth): This plugin reads an API key from a request header and checks it.
- [Basic Auth](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/basic-auth): This plugin checks HTTP Basic credentials (username and password in the Authorization header).
- [Session](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/session): This plugin keeps per-visitor data behind a cookie and exposes it as ctx.session.
- [OIDC](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/oidc): This plugin checks tokens from an OpenID Connect provider, such as Google, Auth0 or Entra ID.
- [Env Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/env): This plugin checks your environment variables when the app starts.

### AI Assistance

- [AI Agent Skills](https://burger-api.com/docs/ai-assistance/agent-skills): Learn how to use Agent Skills to help AI assistants understand your BurgerAPI project structure, APIs, and patterns.

### CLI Tool

- [CLI Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/installation): Install the Burger API CLI to create projects, add hooks and plugins, and build for production.
- [Create Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/create): burger-api create creates a new project and installs its dependencies.
- [Generate Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/generate): burger-api generate (alias g) scaffolds route directories, WebSocket route directories, and local hook/plugin stubs.
- [Add Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/add): burger-api add copies official hooks and plugins into your project.
- [List Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/list): burger-api list (alias ls) shows the official hooks and plugins with a short description of each.
- [Skills Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/skills): burger-api skills adds AI agent skills to your project.
- [Dev Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/dev): burger-api dev runs your app while you develop.
- [Build Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/build): burger-api build builds your app for production.
- [Build Exec Command (build:exec)](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/build-exec): burger-api build:exec builds your app into a single executable file.
- [Inspect Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/inspect): burger-api inspect shows what the CLI finds in your project: your settings, API routes with their methods, pages, WebSocket routes, hooks and plugins.
- [Doctor Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/doctor): burger-api doctor checks your project for common problems.

### Deployment

- [Runtimes & Compatibility](https://burger-api.com/docs/compatibility): You write your app once and run it on Bun in development.
- [Deploy on Bun](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/bun): Bun is BurgerAPI's main runtime (Bun 1.4.4 or newer).
- [Deploy on Node.js](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/node): BurgerAPI runs on Node.js 24 and newer with the @burger-api/node-server package.
- [Deploy on Cloudflare Workers](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/cloudflare): Your BurgerAPI app runs on Cloudflare Workers without code changes.
- [Deploy on Vercel](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/vercel): Your BurgerAPI app runs as a Vercel Function without code changes.
- [Deploy on Deno](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/deno): In October 2026 the Deno team joined Cloudflare.

### Performance

- [Overview](https://burger-api.com/docs/performance/overview): BurgerAPI does most of its work once, when the app starts.

### API Reference

- [Burger](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/burger-class): Burger is your app.
- [Burger Options](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/server-options): new Burger({...}) takes a ServerOptions object.
- [ContextSet](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/context-set): ContextSet is the type of ctx.set.
- [Validation Types](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/validation-types): Type reference for validation.
- [Hook Types](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/hook-types): Type reference for hooks.
- [Request API](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/request-api): Every handler and hook gets ctx, a BurgerContext.
- [Response Mutation](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/response-mutation): Handlers return a standard Response.
- [Route Metadata](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/route-metadata): ctx.route tells you which route handled the request.
- [Query Parsing](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/query-parsing): Read the query string with ctx.query.

### Advanced

- [Testing](https://burger-api.com/docs/advanced/testing): Test routes without a server.
- [Error Handling Patterns](https://burger-api.com/docs/advanced/error-handling): Validation errors: a failed request gets 422 with an RFC 9457 problem details body.
- [Type Safety](https://burger-api.com/docs/advanced/type-safety): TypeScript checks your code before it runs.
- [Benchmarks](https://burger-api.com/docs/advanced/benchmarks): All BurgerAPI benchmarks live in one place: the burger-api-benchmarks repository.
- [Deployment](https://burger-api.com/docs/advanced/deployment): Build your app with burger-api build, then run it on your target.
